claim: BODIR is the smart enemy's horizontal decision, and it is nothing but the facing: it reads PFACE and returns a direction from its sign. There is no toward-the-target term.

source.verbatim: BODIR	LDA	PFACE,U

claim: A negative PFACE branches to BODN1C, the left-hand arm of the decision (PFACE is a flag: 0 = right faced, non-zero = left, RAMDEF.SRC:186).

source.verbatim: BMI	BODN1C

claim: A non-negative PFACE yields joystick direction +1 (move right).

source.verbatim: LDA	#1

claim: A negative PFACE yields joystick direction -1 (move left). DECIMAL: the operand is a bare -1, not a hex byte.

source.verbatim: BODN1C	LDA	#-1

claim: The horizontal-homing throttle: the enemy loads the targeted player's X velocity it holds in PPVELX, under the author's own comment DO NOT COPY PLAYERS MOVES TOO OFTEN.

source.verbatim: BOLEVB	LDA	PPVELX,U	DO NOT COPY PLAYERS MOVES TOO OFTEN

claim: The throttle compares that value against the ENEMY'S OWN velocity index (,U = self, not ,X = the player). The wake counts only when the enemy is already flying its target's speed.

source.verbatim: CMPA	PVELX,U

claim: On a MISMATCH the branch jumps to BODIR3, clear of the counter block entirely: an unmatched wake does not decrement, does not reset, does nothing at all.

source.verbatim: BNE	BODIR3

claim: On a match the reverse-direction counter PRDIR is decremented. DERIVED CADENCE: PRDIR is a single byte (RAMDEF.SRC:208), so from a CLEARED counter this DEC and the BMI on the next line walk 0 -> $FF -> ... -> $80 (128 wakes, every result negative, no flip) and the 129th DEC lands $7F, non-negative, which finally reaches the flip. 129 is DERIVED from the 8-bit wrap and is nowhere stated as a constant in the source. The zero it walks from is the one the flip itself writes at JOUSTRV4.SRC:3944, so 129 is the cadence BETWEEN flips.

source.verbatim: DEC	PRDIR,U

claim: While the decremented counter is still negative the flip is skipped, which is what spreads the reversal over many matched wakes rather than firing on the first.

source.verbatim: BMI	BODIR3

claim: The flip CLEARS the counter back to zero, so every reversal cycle costs the same number of matched wakes as the first.

source.verbatim: CLR	PRDIR,U

claim: The reversal itself is a COMplement of PFACE under the comment TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION: it toggles the facing, it does not aim it at anything.

source.verbatim: COM	PFACE,U		TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION

claim: Control then falls into BODIR, so the newly complemented facing is what BODIR reads on this same wake: the flip steers the current wake, not the next one.

source.verbatim: BODIR3	JMP	BODIR

claim: The hunter (B2) carries the identical throttle block, under the identical comment, so horizontal homing is a per-smart-brain law and not a bounder-only quirk.

source.verbatim: B2LE11	LDA	PPVELX,U	DO NOT COPY PLAYERS MOVES TOO OFTEN

claim: The hunter's reversal is the same COM PFACE,U under the same TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION comment.

source.verbatim: COM	PFACE,U		TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION

claim: The shadow lord carries the same throttle block a third time (its copy uses the long branches LBNE/LBMI, same law, further jump).

source.verbatim: SHLEPB	LDA	PPVELX,U	DO NOT COPY PLAYERS MOVES TOO OFTEN

claim: The shadow lord's reversal is the same COM PFACE,U under the same TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION comment.

source.verbatim: COM	PFACE,U		TRY THE OTHER DIRECTION

claim: The reverse-direction counter is cleared to ZERO on the bird the hatch creates. That bird is the riderless seeker: the same block goes on to hand it PJOY = SEEKE (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3268, thirteen lines further down), so this zero is the seeker's starting value and not the value a mounted enemy's decision routine begins with.

source.verbatim: CLR	PRDIR,Y		ASSUME BIRD NEVER CAME WITHIN SHORT RANGE SCAN

claim: PRDIR is the reverse-direction counter and is ONE byte of RAM. The 8-bit width is load-bearing: modelled as an unbounded integer the counter would never reach a non-negative DEC result and the enemy would never reverse.

source.verbatim: PRDIR	RMB	1		REVERSE DIRECTION COUNTER (FOR EMEMY TRACKING)

claim: PPVELX holds the OLD player X velocity the throttle compares against. It is one byte, and it is written only on entry to level flight (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3907-3908), never inside the throttle itself.

source.verbatim: PPVELX	RMB	1		OLD PLAYERS X VELOCITY (FOR EMEMY TRACKING)

claim: The store that plants the short-range sensor flag in PRDIR on the seeking bird. SEEKFS loads the value on the preceding line; this line commits it to the bird's own workspace, and no branch lies between the two.

source.verbatim: STA	PRDIR,U		THE BIRD CAME WITHIN SHORT RANGE SENSORS

claim: This branch is where a seeking bird gets the man, and it is the only branch to MOUNTM anywhere in the source. So it is the sole route by which a bird ALREADY IN FLIGHT picks up a dismounted man. It is NOT the only way a buzzard comes to carry a rider: an enemy created at a transporter is handed one directly (STD PRIDER,U, JOUSTRV4.SRC:5730) and never passes through here.

source.verbatim: BEQ	MOUNTM		GOT THE MAN!!!

claim: On this arm the enemy loads its intelligence's smart decision routine from DSMART, which the next line installs as the routine its process runs. The arm is conditional: LDA GOVER / BNE 2$ (JOUSTRV4.SRC:3688-3689) reaches it only when the game is NOT over, and the fall-through arm at :3690 loads DJOY instead - a dummie dum dum bird.

source.verbatim: 2$	LDD	DSMART,X	SELECT PROPER JOYSTICK ROUTINE

claim: Process creation ends here, having written only the scheduling fields it names: the free-list link, the nap, the program counter, the process id and the primary/secondary priority. It clears no other byte of the recycled workspace, which is why each creation site clears the fields it cares about one at a time.

source.verbatim: STB	PPRI,Y		NEW - PRIMARY/SECONDARY PROCESS SELECTION

claim: SEEKFS loads the short-range sensor value the next line stores into PRDIR. The value is 1, written in the assembler's bare radix, which for this source is DECIMAL.

source.verbatim: SEEKFS	LDA	#1
